utterances.speaker: Tess
utterances.text: Tess: Hi Kira, have you heard the latest about the repair drive? I’m trying to keep everyone in the loop.

utterances.speaker: Kira
utterances.text: Kira: I’ve heard bits and pieces, Tess, but I’d rather not go on rumors. Can you confirm what’s actually happening and when?

utterances.speaker: Tess
utterances.text: Tess: Fair enough, Kira — what I know for sure is that the repair drive is happening, but I don’t have the confirmed time in hand yet, so I’ll check the noticeboard before I pass anything else along.

utterances.speaker: Vik
utterances.text: Vik: Hey Noah, I heard there’s a repair drive coming up—do you know the plan yet?

utterances.speaker: Noah
utterances.text: Noah: Oh, I heard something about it, but I might’ve missed the details—last I knew they were still figuring out the exact time and what folks should bring.

utterances.speaker: Vik
utterances.text: Vik: Got it, I’ll tell folks the time and bring-list are still being figured out for now. If you hear the final details, let me know and I’ll help spread the word.

utterances.speaker: Leo
utterances.text: Leo: Hey Ira, what repairs are we prioritizing for the drive?

utterances.speaker: Ira
utterances.text: Ira: I’ve only heard bits while I was out, but it sounds like folks are focusing first on safety repairs—leaky roofs, broken steps, and heating issues.

utterances.speaker: Leo
utterances.text: Leo: Got it. I’ll tell people to flag those first and bring any details they have.

utterances.speaker: Rey
utterances.text: Rey: Hey Cleo, I heard a little about the repair drive, but not much yet. What are folks hoping to fix first?

utterances.speaker: Cleo
utterances.text: Cleo: From what I’ve heard, folks want to start with the leaky gutters by the community hall and a couple of broken porch railings. I’m still checking what supplies we’ve actually got on hand.

utterances.speaker: Rey
utterances.text: Rey: That sounds like a sensible place to start. If you find out what supplies are missing, I can quietly ask around and see who might have extras.

utterances.speaker: Faye
utterances.text: Faye: Hi Jules, I’m trying to line up the repair drive around school pickup and drop-off—do you know what time folks are planning to start?

utterances.speaker: Jules
utterances.text: Jules: Hey Faye! I haven’t heard a firm start time yet, but I can check with a couple of folks and see what’s easiest around pickup and drop-off.

utterances.speaker: Faye
utterances.text: Faye: Thanks, Jules — if it helps, I can cover a late-morning slot after drop-off, but I’ll need to duck out before pickup.

utterances.speaker: Eli
utterances.text: Eli: Morning, Oren. If we’re doing this repair drive, I’d like us to set a simple schedule and a clear list of what needs fixing first.

utterances.speaker: Oren
utterances.text: Oren: Morning, Eli—yes, a simple schedule would help me not lose the thread. Let’s start with the urgent fixes first, and maybe you can remind me what’s already on the list?

utterances.speaker: Eli
utterances.text: Eli: Good—let’s write it down plainly: urgent items first, then the smaller repairs after. I’ve got no list in front of me yet, so let’s start with whatever folks have already reported.

utterances.speaker: Quinn
utterances.text: Quinn: Hey Pia, I’m glad I caught you—there’s a repair drive coming together, and I’m trying to spread the word fast. Want me to save you a spot or pass along the details?

utterances.speaker: Pia
utterances.text: Pia: Oh, maybe, but I’d need the details first—where is it, what time, and do we have to bring tools or sign up ahead?

utterances.speaker: Quinn
utterances.text: Quinn: I’m still getting the final details, but I’ll check right away and send you the time, place, and whether tools or signup are needed as soon as I have them.

utterances.speaker: Nell
utterances.text: Nell: Hi Rosa, I’ve only heard bits and pieces about the repair drive—do you know what still needs fixing or who’s organizing it?

utterances.speaker: Rosa
utterances.text: Rosa: Hi Nell! I’m helping coordinate it, and we’re still making the list—so far it’s mostly loose porch rails, a few broken lights, and some garden tools that need repair.

utterances.speaker: Nell
utterances.text: Nell: Oh, that’s helpful—thanks, Rosa. If you need another set of hands for checking the list or passing along updates, I’d be glad to help.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Hana: Hi Mara, I’m glad we’re talking about the repair drive—can you walk me through what’s already confirmed and what still needs deciding?

utterances.speaker: Mara
utterances.text: Mara: Sure — as far as I know, nothing is firmly confirmed yet, so we should pin down the date, location, volunteer roles, and what kinds of repairs we’ll accept.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Hana: Thanks, that helps—let’s start by choosing two or three possible dates and a location option before we ask volunteers to commit.

utterances.speaker: Uli
utterances.text: Uli: I can help a little with the repair drive, Dane. I’m not up for much talking, but I can sort parts or carry things if you need.

utterances.speaker: Dane
utterances.text: Dane: That’d be a real help, Uli—sorting parts is perfect, and no need to do much talking. I’ll probably arrive a bit late, but I’ll point you to the boxes when I get there.

utterances.speaker: Uli
utterances.text: Uli: That’s fine. I’ll wait near the boxes and just start where you point me.

utterances.speaker: Gus
utterances.text: Gus: Hey Mina, I’ve got a couple toolboxes and a cordless drill I can bring for the repair drive if that helps.

utterances.speaker: Mina
utterances.text: Mina: That helps, Gus. Can you bring extra drill bits and label your toolboxes so nothing gets mixed up?

utterances.speaker: Gus
utterances.text: Gus: Absolutely, I’ll pack the extra bits and put clear labels on both toolboxes before I bring them over.

utterances.speaker: Opal
utterances.text: Opal: Hi Bo, I’m just getting my notes started for the repair drive—do we know where the drop-off table and tool station will be set up?

utterances.speaker: Bo
utterances.text: Bo: I only skimmed the notice, but I think the drop-off table’s by the community room entrance and the tools are supposed to be inside near the back wall.

utterances.speaker: Opal
utterances.text: Opal: Thanks, Bo—I’ll mark the drop-off table by the community room entrance and the tool station inside near the back wall, with a note that it’s not fully confirmed yet.

utterances.speaker: Gus
utterances.text: Gus: Hey Rey, I was thinking I could bring over my socket set and cordless drill for the repair drive—anything specific you need help rounding up?

utterances.speaker: Rey
utterances.text: Rey: That’d be a big help, Gus. If you’ve got any spare bits, tape, or small clamps, those always seem to disappear fast at these things.

utterances.speaker: Gus
utterances.text: Gus: You got it, I’ll toss in my bit case, a couple rolls of tape, and whatever small clamps I can spare.

utterances.speaker: Pia
utterances.text: Pia: I’m glad we’re doing the repair drive, but I want to make sure we’ve got the drop-off times, volunteers, and storage sorted before we announce anything.

utterances.speaker: Kira
utterances.text: Kira: I’m on board, but can we confirm the exact drop-off hours and who’s actually covering each shift before we tell the neighborhood?

utterances.speaker: Pia
utterances.text: Pia: Yes, exactly—let’s make a simple shift list first and only announce the hours once we know we have coverage and a dry place to store everything.

utterances.speaker: Jules
utterances.text: Jules: Hey Mara, I was thinking the repair drive could be a great chance to bring a few of our different circles together. What kind of help are you hoping to line up first?

utterances.speaker: Mara
utterances.text: Mara: I’d love to start by finding a couple of handy fixers and someone organized to help triage items as folks arrive. If we get that core in place, it’ll be much easier to invite the wider circles in.

utterances.speaker: Jules
utterances.text: Jules: That makes sense — I can ask around for two handy folks and think of someone calm and organized for triage. Once we’ve got those names, we can start pulling in the wider groups.

utterances.speaker: Cleo
utterances.text: Cleo: Hey Dane, I’m glad we’re talking about the repair drive—do we already have a list of what supplies folks need most?

utterances.speaker: Dane
utterances.text: Dane: I’m not sure yet—I’m joining a bit late, but I can help pull together a quick needs list if folks have been mentioning items already.

utterances.speaker: Cleo
utterances.text: Cleo: That would be a big help—let’s start with basics like screws, tape, gloves, extension cords, and any tool shortages people mention.

utterances.speaker: Tess
utterances.text: Tess: Oh Faye, I was just hoping to catch you—have you heard when the repair drive is supposed to start?

utterances.speaker: Faye
utterances.text: Faye: I haven’t heard the exact start time yet, but I can check after school pickup and let you know.

utterances.speaker: Tess
utterances.text: Tess: Oh, that’d be wonderful, thank you—I’ll keep an ear out too and let you know if I hear anything first.

utterances.speaker: Bo
utterances.text: Bo: Hey Rosa, I’m a bit swamped, but I heard there’s a repair drive coming up—what’s the quick version?

utterances.speaker: Rosa
utterances.text: Rosa: Quick version: we’re collecting small broken household items this Saturday at the community room, and neighbors with repair skills will help fix what they can. If you’re swamped, just swing by with one item or help spread the word.

utterances.speaker: Bo
utterances.text: Bo: Got it—Saturday at the community room, small broken stuff, and spread the word if I can. I’ll mention it to a couple folks and maybe bring my busted toaster.

utterances.speaker: Sam
utterances.text: Sam: Hey Leo, I’m glad you brought up the repair drive — I’d be happy to help however I can. What still needs doing?

utterances.speaker: Leo
utterances.text: Leo: Thanks, Sam. We still need someone to sort tools and make a simple sign-up sheet.

utterances.speaker: Sam
utterances.text: Sam: I can take care of both—I'll sort the tools and put together a simple sign-up sheet before the drive.

utterances.speaker: Quinn
utterances.text: Quinn: Hey Nell, I’m glad I caught you—there’s a repair drive coming together, and I’m trying to make sure everyone nearby hears about it.

utterances.speaker: Nell
utterances.text: Nell: Oh, thanks for letting me know, Quinn—I hadn’t heard about it yet. What kind of repairs are they collecting for?

utterances.speaker: Quinn
utterances.text: Quinn: They’re gathering small household fixes—things like wobbly chairs, torn jackets, lamps, and bikes—so folks with repair skills can help patch them up together.

utterances.speaker: Opal
utterances.text: Opal: I’m keeping track of where everything’s headed for the repair drive. Tell me which location you need next, and I’ll note it down.

utterances.speaker: Eli
utterances.text: Eli: Let’s keep it simple, Opal—please note the community center as the next location. I’ll plan to bring my box there Tuesday morning.

utterances.speaker: Opal
utterances.text: Opal: Got it, Eli—I’ll note the community center as the next location, with your box planned for Tuesday morning.

utterances.speaker: Mina
utterances.text: Mina: Hana, what repairs are we prioritizing first, and how many volunteers do we actually have?

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Hana: Let me confirm the list before we lock it in—are the roof leaks and broken steps still the most urgent, and do we have a current volunteer count from last night’s sign-up sheet?

utterances.speaker: Mina
utterances.text: Mina: Yes, roof leaks and broken steps are still first. I don’t have the final count yet—can you check the sign-up sheet and tell me how many can work Saturday?

utterances.speaker: Ira
utterances.text: Ira: Hey Oren, I’m just catching up while I’m out—what’s the latest on the repair drive?

utterances.speaker: Oren
utterances.text: Oren: Oh, hi Ira—last I heard, folks were still gathering broken lamps and small appliances, but I might be a bit fuzzy on the drop-off time. I can double-check and let you know if you want.

utterances.speaker: Ira
utterances.text: Ira: Thanks, Oren—that’d be great. I’ll keep an ear out too while I’m running errands.

utterances.speaker: Pia
utterances.text: Pia: Before we promise anything, do we know where the repair tables would go and who’s handling sign-ups?

utterances.speaker: Rey
utterances.text: Rey: Not yet, I don’t think. I can ask around quietly and see who has space for tables, but we should probably name one person for sign-ups before we announce it.

utterances.speaker: Pia
utterances.text: Pia: That sounds sensible; if you check on table space, I can make a short list of what sign-ups would need so we don’t get swamped.

utterances.speaker: Tess
utterances.text: Tess: Oh Quinn, I’m glad I caught you—are you helping with the repair drive, or just trying to figure out what all the fuss is about?

utterances.speaker: Quinn
utterances.text: Quinn: A bit of both, honestly—but if there’s a repair drive happening, you know I’m already thinking who on the block needs to hear about it first.

utterances.speaker: Tess
utterances.text: Tess: That’s exactly why I came to you—Marla’s toaster’s been dead for weeks, and I heard Mr. Iqbal’s got a lamp he keeps meaning to fix.

utterances.speaker: Nell
utterances.text: Nell: Hi Jules, I’ve only heard bits and pieces about the repair drive—what’s the latest?

utterances.speaker: Jules
utterances.text: Jules: Hey Nell! We’re pulling folks together for a neighborhood repair drive this weekend—people can bring small broken items, and I’m matching up anyone with handy skills to help out.

utterances.speaker: Nell
utterances.text: Nell: That sounds really useful—do you still need people to help organize or spread the word, even if they’re not especially handy?

utterances.speaker: Vik
utterances.text: Vik: Hey Dane, I heard there’s a repair drive coming together—what’s the plan so far?

utterances.speaker: Dane
utterances.text: Dane: Hey Vik—I'm just catching up myself, but it sounds like folks are gathering broken small appliances and tools first, then lining up volunteers to help fix them.

utterances.speaker: Vik
utterances.text: Vik: Got it—collect the broken appliances and tools first, then find volunteers to repair them. I’ll pass that along if anyone asks.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Hana: Before we start, Bo, can you tell me which repairs are most urgent and who’s already offered to help?

utterances.speaker: Bo
utterances.text: Bo: I only skimmed the notes, honestly—urgent ones look like the community room leak and the broken front steps. I know Mara offered tools, and I think Ken said he could help Saturday.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Hana: Thanks, Bo — I’ll mark the leak and front steps as priority, but I want to confirm Ken for Saturday before counting on him. Do you know where the notes are so I can double-check?

utterances.speaker: Rosa
utterances.text: Rosa: Hi Kira, I’m glad we’re getting the repair drive moving—do you have a sense of what items neighbors most need help fixing?

utterances.speaker: Kira
utterances.text: Kira: I’m not sure yet, Rosa—have we actually checked with the neighbors, or are we just guessing from what people mentioned in passing?

utterances.speaker: Rosa
utterances.text: Rosa: You’re right, Kira—we shouldn’t guess. I’ll put together a quick sign-up sheet and ask folks on the block what they actually need repaired before we set the list.

utterances.speaker: Eli
utterances.text: Eli: Morning, Sam. If we’re doing this repair drive, I’d like us to set a clear date, a drop-off spot, and a list of what we can actually fix.

utterances.speaker: Sam
utterances.text: Sam: Morning, Eli — agreed. Let’s pick a Saturday, use my garage as the drop-off spot if that works, and I’ll help make a simple list of items we can safely handle.

utterances.speaker: Eli
utterances.text: Eli: That works for me, Sam. Let’s choose next Saturday, put your garage down as the drop-off spot, and keep the fix list to lamps, small appliances, and simple furniture repairs.

utterances.speaker: Faye
utterances.text: Faye: Hi Mina, I’m happy to help with the repair drive—do we know yet if it’s happening before or after school pickup?

utterances.speaker: Mina
utterances.text: Mina: Not yet—can you do either, or do you need us to pick a time now?

utterances.speaker: Faye
utterances.text: Faye: I can do either, but after pickup is easier for me since I’ll already be near the school with the kids.

utterances.speaker: Oren
utterances.text: Oren: Hi Opal, remind me—are we collecting tools for the repair drive today, or was I supposed to bring something else?

utterances.speaker: Opal
utterances.text: Opal: Yes, today is tool collection for the repair drive—bring any working hand tools you can spare, and I’ll note who dropped off what.

utterances.speaker: Oren
utterances.text: Oren: Right, tools today—thanks, Opal. I’ll bring over my spare hammer and a couple screwdrivers before I forget again.

utterances.speaker: Ira
utterances.text: Ira: Hey Noah, I’ve been out running errands—what’s the latest on the repair drive?

utterances.speaker: Noah
utterances.text: Noah: Honestly, Ira, I’m a little behind on the latest myself—I must’ve missed the last update. I can ask around and let you know what I hear.

utterances.speaker: Ira
utterances.text: Ira: Thanks, Noah, I’d appreciate that—if I hear anything while I’m out, I’ll pass it along too.

utterances.speaker: Cleo
utterances.text: Cleo: Hey Mara, I’m starting a quick list of what we’ve got for the repair drive—tools, tape, spare parts, that sort of thing. What supplies do you know we already have?

utterances.speaker: Mara
utterances.text: Mara: I don’t have a confirmed list yet, Cleo, but I can check with folks and make sure we don’t double-count anything.

utterances.speaker: Cleo
utterances.text: Cleo: Thanks, Mara—if you can ask around, I’ll keep the list open and mark everything as unconfirmed until we hear back.

utterances.speaker: Gus
utterances.text: Gus: Hey Leo, I was thinking I could bring over my tool chest and a couple extension cords for the repair drive. What do you reckon folks will need most?

utterances.speaker: Leo
utterances.text: Leo: That sounds useful, Gus. Most folks will probably need screwdrivers, pliers, a drill, and maybe a few spare fasteners or tape.

utterances.speaker: Gus
utterances.text: Gus: Perfect, I’ll pack the screwdrivers, pliers, drill, and a bin of screws and tape, then. I’ll swing by a little early to help set up.
